summary: Mid-cycle credit reversal and proration question for monthly committed plan
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a credit applied on 2026-03-05 for overage was unexpectedly reversed in the middle of the billing cycle (2026-03-10), and invoice/proration lines do not match the expected committed plan proration rules.

Impact: Finance team at FluxHealth has halted their internal reconciliation. The customer reports a negative credit balance on the console and an unexpected change in the estimated monthly spend that could trigger internal alerts. No service degradation reported; only billing and metering visibility affected.

Environment: Dedicated account on prod/us-east, reserved monthly committed plan (3x A100 equivalent). Usage spikes were common during 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-07 for a migration test.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Navigate to Console -> Billing -> Billing History for March 2026
2) Observe credit line posted on 2026-03-05 ("overage credit - manual review") for -$1,420.00
3) Refresh 2026-03-10 and note a line item "credit reversal - reconciliation" for +$1,420.00 and a corresponding negative estimated balance.
4) Check Invoices -> Invoice #FH-2026-03 and see proration lines that seem to double-count a partial month adjustment.

Logs / artifacts provided:
- Screenshots of billing history (attached to Jira ticket link).
- CSV export of usage and billing lines (customer_uploaded_FluxHealth_Mar.csv).
- Support-run billing export from 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-12 (attached).

Initial hypothesis: There may have been a mid-cycle reconciliation job that attempted to correct an earlier manual credit but applied the inverse entry instead of adjusting the proration, or a webhook from the finance team created a reversing journal. Alternatively, a previous charge was reclassified resulting in automated reversal.

Requested outcome: Customer requests (1) explanation of the reversal origin, (2) correction if this was applied in error, (3) an adjusted invoice or credit memo so their accounting team can close the month, and (4) a short runbook explaining how mid-cycle credits/prorations appear in the console to avoid future confusion.
comments: 2026-03-11 15:22 - Aisha Patel (support): Created ticket after receiving email from FluxHealth finance contact (j.meyer@fluxhealth.com). Requested csv and screenshots of billing lines. Marked as Sev2 due to financial reconciliation impact.

2026-03-11 17:05 - Marcus Lee (billing eng): I'm pulling the billing ledger for FluxHealth and will cross-check the journal entries and any automated reconciliation jobs that ran between 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-11. Assigned to me for deeper investigation.

2026-03-12 09:40 - Marcus Lee (billing eng): Preliminary findings: There is an automated end-of-day reconciliation job (job-id reconcile-2026-03-10) that attempted to re-evaluate manual credits older than 72h. It emitted a reversal journal for entry jrn-5582 but the reversal was posted as a positive line item and a second adjustment was posted to proration lines. Extracts attached: reconcile-log-2026-03-10.txt. Flagging accounting for review.
Suggested next step: Hold any further automated reconcile runs for this account and escalate to Finance Ops to validate the intended logic for manual credits older than 72h.

2026-03-12 12:18 - Finance Ops (comment): We see a codepath where manual credits created via the Console UI flow 'manual_credit_v1' are later re-evaluated by 'reconcile-legacy' to prevent duplicate credits across mid-cycle plan changes. It appears the reconciliation determined the original manual credit should not have applied under the new proration model and therefore reversed it. However, the reversal journal was constructed incorrectly (sign inversion) and the proration adjustment was applied twice. Root cause likely a data-mapping bug in reconcile-legacy. Creating INT-452 to patch the job and roll forward corrective journal entries.

2026-03-12 16:02 - Marcus Lee (billing eng): Reached out to FluxHealth to confirm acceptable remediation: (A) Create a corrective credit memo for -$1,420.00 with note 'manual credit reinstated pending reconcile fix' and (B) re-run proration calc to regenerate invoice lines. Customer acknowledged preferred option A+B.
FluxHealth (J. Meyer) replied: 'We need a corrected invoice before EOD 2026-03-13 if possible; otherwise we'll escalate to procurement.'

2026-03-13 08:30 - Aisha Patel (support): Escalating to Finance Ops and assigning INT-452 (linked). Notified SRE to pause reconcile-legacy for the dedicated cluster for FluxHealth until the fix is deployed. Added label urgent.
resolution: Investigation in progress; Finance Ops acknowledged a bug in reconcile-legacy leading to sign inversion and duplicate proration. Planned remediation: pause job, create corrective credit memo and regenerated invoice lines. INT-452 opened to fix reconcile-legacy mapping; accounting will issue credit memo by 2026-03-13 EOD per customer request.
